BiblicalUsage: Baal-gad was a town in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon, at the northern edge of the conquest — the limit of the land Joshua took, from Baal-gad in the valley to Mount Halak. Joshua names it three times, always as a boundary: the war ended there, and the inheritance began.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the northern boundary matters because it shows the conquest was finished and measured — God gave the land, and he gave it with edges.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
